modern: A spider is proud when it has caught a fly, and another when he has caught a poor hare, and another when he has taken a little fish in a net, and another when he has taken wild boars, and another when he has taken bears, and another when he has taken Sarmatians. Are these not robbers, if you examine their opinions?

explained.summary: Pride in a catch depends on what you’ve caught. A spider is pleased with a fly, a hunter with a hare or a bear, a general with a defeated people. Marcus includes himself here: the Sarmatians were a people he spent years fighting on Rome’s Danube frontier. Look honestly at the motives, he says, and the conqueror is only a grander kind of robber.
